record.paper_title: Eight Open Problems in Distributed Computing
record.context_brief: Stability bounds for memoryless symmetric consensus
record.original_question: For memoryless symmetric ongoing consensus functions, where the function output is invariant under permutations of input positions, how can the approximately factor-2 gap between known upper and lower bounds on the number of output changes be closed, and how should non-geodesic input-change paths be analyzed to distinguish and evaluate the performance of different consensus functions?

evidence.quote: An upper bound for the number of output changes for a memoryless symmetric system (where the function has the same output regardless of the position of inputs in the input vector) is presented in [20].
Closing this gap, as well as considering non geodesic input path changes that are useful to separate the performance and to evaluate consensus functions are open questions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the long-lived consensus problem in the following abstract form. Let $n \ge 1$ and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function that is symmetric, i.e. invariant under all permutations of its $n$ input coordinates: $f(x_{\sigma(1)}, \dots, x_{\sigma(n)}) = f(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ for every permutation $\sigma \in S_n$. The function $f$ is interpreted as a memoryless consensus rule: at each time step $t$, given an input vector $x^{(t)} \in \{0,1\}^n$, the system outputs $f(x^{(t)})$, with no dependence on past inputs or outputs.

Given an input path, that is a sequence $x^{(0)}, x^{(1)}, \dots, x^{(T)} \in \{0,1\}^n$ in which consecutive vectors differ in at most one coordinate, define the number of output changes along the path as
$$ \mathrm{OC}(f; x^{(0)},\dots,x^{(T)}) \;=\; \#\bigl\{\, t \in \{1,\dots,T\} : f(x^{(t)}) \neq f(x^{(t-1)}) \,\bigr\}. $$
A path is called geodesic if it realizes the Hamming distance between its endpoints, i.e. $T = \|x^{(T)} - x^{(0)}\|_1$ and no coordinate is flipped more than once.

The "instability" of $f$ is the worst-case rate of output changes over admissible input paths. Known results provide an upper bound $U(n)$ and a lower bound $L(n)$ on this instability for symmetric memoryless rules, valid uniformly over $f$, with $U(n)/L(n)$ tending to a constant approximately equal to $2$ as $n \to \infty$.

(a) Determine the exact asymptotic instability of memoryless symmetric consensus, thereby closing the factor-$2$ gap between $U(n)$ and $L(n)$.

(b) Extend the analysis to non-geodesic input paths (paths in which coordinates may be flipped repeatedly) and develop quantitative measures based on such paths that distinguish and rank different symmetric consensus functions $f$ according to their output-change behavior.
artifact.status_search_result: Related work (e.g., Davidovitch–Dolev–Rajsbaum on stability of long-lived consensus and a 2011 arXiv preprint "Geodesic stability for memoryless binary long-lived consensus") addresses bounds on output changes for symmetric memoryless consensus, but no source found indicates the factor-2 gap has been closed or that a non-geodesic-path framework for separating consensus functions has been developed. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic stability for memoryless binary long-lived consensus
status_evidence.snippet: Studies stability bounds along geodesic input-change paths for symmetric memoryless consensus rules.
status_evidence.claim: Existing bounds are stated along geodesic paths, leaving non-geodesic analyses and gap-closing as further questions.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Long-lived Consensus
status_evidence.snippet: Provides upper and lower bounds for stability of symmetric memoryless consensus systems.
status_evidence.claim: Original bounds with a constant-factor gap appear here; no later work surfaced that closes the gap.
